plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq, batch-confounded DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000 x 12 gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, salmon gene counts as delivered) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition, batch) from human lung, 6 treated vs 6 control. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control. The decisive design fact is in the profile: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 holds all 6 treated samples, so processing batch is perfectly confounded with condition. The model matrix for ~ batch + condition is not full rank, and ComBat-seq / removeBatchEffect / SVA would strip the condition effect along with the batch. Therefore the plan fits ~ condition alone, never a batch term and never a batch-removal step, and every result is labelled confounded: the estimated treated-vs-control effect is the sum of the true treatment effect and any B2-vs-B1 processing effect, and the two are not separable from these data. T1S1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by both condition and batch — this documents the confounding rather than resolving it, since condition and batch label the same partition. T1S2 fits DESeq2 (minimal pre-filter of 10 counts in at least 6 samples, median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on) on the counts as delivered with no length offset: the profile states the record does not say whether salmon's length correction was applied, and no quant.sf files or average transcript length table are present, so tximport must not be run on a gene table and the lost length offset must be declared as a caveat (a shift in isoform usage can present as differential expression). T1S3 repeats the same contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as an independent second method; the intersection is the high-confidence set. T1S4 assembles the report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, the gene table with unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold changes and lfcSE, the two-method overlap, and a prominent statement that no gene call can be attributed to treatment rather than to batch. No enrichment step is planned — the question asks only which genes differ, and pathway interpretation of a fully confounded contrast would compound the problem.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
median-of-ratios size factors inside the model
~ condition only, no batch term (batch perfectly confounded)
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (second method for robustness overlap)
confounded-labelled DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, method overlap

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; its contents follow the reporting claims R-0085/R-0087/R-0042/R-0041/R-0086, plus the confounded labelling required by the R-0005@668f flag.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If the batch is perfectly confounded with the condition, do not fit a batch term and do not adjust the counts with ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or a surrogate variable method. The model matrix is not full rank, and a removal method would remove the condition effect with the batch. State the assumption of no batch effect and label every result as confounded, or stop and ask for a design where the batches hold every condition.
